news.titleTr: Nvidia'da kriz derinleşiyor: İlişki skandalı Huawei'ye uzandı
news.summaryTr: Nvidia'nın eski CEO'su Jensen Huang ile ilişkisi olduğu bildirilen Alice Huang'ın, şirketin Çinli rakibi Huawei'ye fayda sağlayan işletmelerde pay sahibi olduğu öne sürüldü. 7,5 milyar dolarlık çip sevkiyatına uzanan bağlantılar, ulusal güvenlik soruşturması çağrısını gündeme getirdi.
news.articleText: Nvidia'da kriz derinleşiyor: İlişki skandalı Huawei'ye uzandı - Nvidia'nın eski CEO'su Jensen Huang ile ilişkisi olduğu bildirilen Alice Huang'ın, şirketin Çinli rakibi Huawei'ye fayda sağlayan işletmelerde pay sahibi olduğu öne sürüldü. 7,5 milyar dolarlık çip sevkiyatına uzanan bağlantılar, ulusal güvenlik soruşturması çağrısını gündeme getirdi. Nvidia'nın görevinden ayrılan CEO'su Jensen Huang ile ilişkisi olduğu bildirilen Alice Huang hakkında yeni iddialar gündeme geldi. CNBC'nin haberine göre Alice Huang'ın, Nvidia'nın Çin'deki en büyük rakiplerinden Huawei'ye fayda sağlayan şirketlerde pay sahibi olduğu öne sürüldü. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Özel istihbarat şirketi Tesari'nin analistleri tarafından ortaya çıkarılan bağlantılar, Nvidia'nın Çin'e yönelik çip sevkiyatlarına ilişkin tartışmaları yeniden alevlendirdi. ABD istihbaratının Çin adına casusluk yaptığını iddia ettiği bildirilen Alice Huang'ın, söz konusu şirketlerde Nvidia ile iş yaptığı dönemde pay sahibi olmuş olabileceği belirtildi. 7,5 milyar dolarlık çip sevkiyatı Tesari'nin derlediği şirket kayıtlarına göre Alice Huang, sahibi olduğu Osmanthus adlı bulut bilişim şirketini 2019'da Çinli oyun şirketi 7Road'a sattı. 7Road'un Singapur merkezli bir iştiraki 2023'te Megaspeed adıyla ayrıldı. The Information'ın haberine göre Nvidia'nın önemli müşterilerinden biri haline gelen Megaspeed, Çinli şirketlere en az 7,5 milyar dolarlık Nvidia çipi sevkiyatına aracılık etti. Huawei'ye uzanan yatırım ağı Alice Huang'ın ortağı olduğu Shanghai Hexi adlı finans şirketi, 2021 yılında veri merkezi geliştiricisi Shanghai Century Longteng'in yüzde 27'sini satın aldı. Shanghai Century Longteng'in kontrolündeki Shenzhen Yifeng Technology veri merkezinin kilit müşterisinin Huawei Cloud olduğu belirtildi. Shanghai Hexi'nin ayrıca tesisin finansmanı için kullanılan kredilere kefil olduğu bildirildi. CNBC'nin incelediği belgelere göre Alice Huang ile bağlantılı işletmeler, Aralık 2023 döneminde Huawei'ye Nvidia teknolojisine dayalı bilgi işlem gücü sağlanmasıyla ilişkilendirildi. Ulusal güvenlik soruşturması çağrısı Tesari yöneticisi Brian Andersen, söz konusu bağlantıların ulusal güvenlik kapsamında soruşturulması gerektiğini belirtti. Andersen, ihracat kontrolüne tabi ekipmanların Huawei'ye izinsiz aktarıldığının kanıtlanması halinde ihracat kontrolü ihlali, komplo ve kaçakçılık suçlamalarının gündeme gelebileceğini söyledi. Tesari analistleri ise şirketler arasındaki bağlantıların, ilişkileri gizlemek amacıyla yapılandırılmış olabileceğinden şüphelendiklerini aktardı.

news.title: S&P, Arçelik'in kredi notunu düşürdü: 2027 için dikkat çeken tahmin
news.summary: S&P Global Ratings, Arçelik'in kredi notunu "B+"dan "B"ye indirirken negatif görünümü korudu. Şirketin 2026'da negatif nakit akışı kaydetmesini bekleyen kuruluş, 2027'de ise 3-4 milyar TL'ye kadar pozitif serbest faaliyet nakit akışı yaratabileceğini öngördü.

news.titleTr: S&P, Arçelik'in kredi notunu düşürdü: 2027 için dikkat çeken tahmin
news.summaryTr: S&P Global Ratings, Arçelik'in kredi notunu "B+"dan "B"ye indirirken negatif görünümü korudu. Şirketin 2026'da negatif nakit akışı kaydetmesini bekleyen kuruluş, 2027'de ise 3-4 milyar TL'ye kadar pozitif serbest faaliyet nakit akışı yaratabileceğini öngördü.
news.articleText: S&P, Arçelik'in kredi notunu düşürdü: 2027 için dikkat çeken tahmin - S&P Global Ratings, Arçelik'in kredi notunu "B+"dan "B"ye indirirken negatif görünümü korudu. Şirketin 2026'da negatif nakit akışı kaydetmesini bekleyen kuruluş, 2027'de ise 3-4 milyar TL'ye kadar pozitif serbest faaliyet nakit akışı yaratabileceğini öngördü. Uluslararası kredi derecelendirme kuruluşu S&P Global Ratings, Arçelik'in uzun vadeli kredi notunu "B+"dan "B"ye düşürürken, not görünümünü "Negatif" olarak korudu. Kuruluş, zayıf tüketici talebi, fiyat baskıları ve yüksek finansman maliyetlerinin şirketin finansal performansı üzerindeki etkisine dikkat çekti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Arçelik'in Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) yaptığı açıklamaya göre, S&P Global Ratings şirketin uzun vadeli kredi notunu bir kademe indirdi. Kuruluş, Arçelik'in Eylül 2028 vadeli 500 milyon dolarlık tahvillerinin kredi notunu da "B"den "B-"ye çekti. S&P, beyaz eşya sektöründeki zorlu koşulların şirketin kârlılığını, nakit yaratma kapasitesini ve borç ödeme gücünü olumsuz etkilediğini belirtti. Gelirler yüzde 12, FAVÖK yüzde 29 geriledi Derecelendirme kuruluşu, Arçelik'in 2026 yılının ilk dokuz ayındaki finansal sonuçlarının beklentilerinin altında kaldığını bildirdi. Şirketin Türk lirası bazında reel gelirleri yüzde 12, faiz, amortisman ve vergi öncesi kârı (FAVÖK) ise yüzde 29 azaldı. Üçüncü çeyrekte gelirlerdeki yıllık düşüş yüzde 14 olurken, FAVÖK'teki gerileme yüzde 47'ye ulaştı. Arçelik'in toplam gelirlerinin yüzde 65'ini oluşturan uluslararası pazarlarda satışlar yaklaşık yüzde 18 düşerken, Türkiye'deki satışlarda yüzde 4,5'lik gerileme kaydedildi. Uluslararası pazarlarda yıllık büyüme gösteren tek bölge Afrika ve Orta Doğu oldu. S&P, şirketin Türkiye'de satış hacmini artırarak pazar liderliğini sürdürdüğünü ancak hacim artışında promosyonların etkili olduğunu belirtti. Toplam gelirlerin yüzde 48'inin elde edildiği Avrupa'da ise özellikle Batı Avrupa'da Beko'nun pazar payının baskı altında kaldığına işaret edildi. Buna karşın markanın Euromonitor verilerine göre yüzde 19'luk hacim payını koruduğu aktarıldı. Kârlılıkta düşüş beklentisi S&P, Arçelik'in 2026 yılı gelirlerinin enflasyon muhasebesi sonrasında 595-597 milyar TL aralığında gerçekleşmesini bekliyor. Şirketin 2025 yılı geliri 523,9 milyar TL olmuştu. Kuruluş, 2025'te yüzde 4,8 olan düzeltilmiş FAVÖK marjının bu yıl yüzde 4'ün altına inebileceğini öngördü. S&P, söz konusu oranın sektörün yüzde 6-9 aralığındaki ortalamasının ve Whirlpool ile Electrolux gibi rakiplerin kârlılık seviyelerinin altında kaldığını vurguladı. Arçelik'in düzeltilmiş FAVÖK'ünün faiz giderlerini karşılama oranının 1 katın biraz altında kalması beklenirken, 2026 yılı serbest faaliyet nakit akışının 6,5-8,5 milyar TL negatif gerçekleşebileceği tahmin edildi. Yatırım harcamalarındaki düşüşe rağmen yüksek finansman giderleri ve zayıf kârlılığın nakit akışı üzerindeki baskıyı sürdüreceği belirtildi. Hitachi ortaklığındaki satış borç azaltımına katkı sağlayacak S&P, Arçelik yönetiminin borç seviyesini düşürmek, kârlılığı artırmak ve nakit akışını güçlendirmek için yürüttüğü çalışmalara da değerlendirmesinde yer verdi. Şirketin Hitachi ile ortak girişimindeki yüzde 60 payını satmasıyla yaklaşık 205 milyon dolarlık peşin nakit girişi sağlaması bekleniyor. İşlem kapsamında sonraki üç yıl içerisinde 56 milyon dolarlık ilave ödeme yapılması öngörülüyor. Derecelendirme kuruluşu, satıştan elde edilecek kaynakların tamamının borç ödemelerinde kullanılacağını ve işlemin 2027 yılında şirketin borçluluğunu azaltmasına katkı sağlayacağını tahmin ediyor. S&P'nin 2027 yılı beklentileri arasında borçluluk oranının 8 kata kadar gerilemesi, düzeltilmiş FAVÖK marjının yüzde 3,6-3,7 seviyesinde gerçekleşmesi ve 3-4 milyar TL'ye kadar pozitif serbest faaliyet nakit akışı bulunuyor. LG ile klima faaliyetlerine yönelik tedarik koşullarında yapılan değişikliklerin de işletme sermayesi yönetimini desteklemesi bekleniyor. Koç Holding desteği değerlendirmede öne çıktı S&P, Arçelik'in negatif nakit akışına ve yüksek finansman maliyetlerine rağmen günlük operasyonlarını finanse edebilecek durumda olduğunu bildirdi. Kuruluş, şirketin Eylül 2028 vadeli 500 milyon dolarlık tahvillerine ilişkin refinansman riskini görece düşük değerlendirirken, bu görüşünde çoğunluk hissedarı Koç Holding'in güçlü finansal yapısını ve geçmişte sağladığı desteği dikkate aldı. Koç Holding'in net nakit pozisyonuna sahip olduğu belirtilirken, holdingin Arçelik'e yönelik son desteğinin 2025 yılında gerçekleştirdiği hisse alımı olduğu hatırlatıldı. Yeni not indirimi riski sürüyor S&P, negatif görünümün Arçelik'in önümüzdeki 12-18 aylık finansal performansına ilişkin aşağı yönlü riskleri yansıttığını açıkladı. Kuruluş, tüketici talebindeki zayıflığın ve yüksek borçlanma maliyetlerinin varlık satışları ile maliyet azaltıcı önlemlerden sağlanacak faydaları sınırlayabileceğini belirtti. Arçelik'in operasyonel performansında yeterli iyileşme sağlayamaması, FAVÖK faiz karşılama oranının 1 katın altında kalmaya devam etmesi ve likidite pozisyonunun zayıflaması halinde yeni bir kredi notu indiriminin gündeme gelebileceği bildirildi. Ana hissedar desteğinin de olası bir not kararında etkili olacağı kaydedildi. S&P, şirketin kârlılığını ve nakit akışını güçlendirerek faiz karşılama oranını 1 katın üzerine çıkarması durumunda ise not görünümünün "Durağan"a çevrilebileceğini ifade etti.

news.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy

news.titleTr: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
news.summaryTr: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs.
news.articleText: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy - Published Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December. Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X. "The American people deserve answers," he added. Scott asked Huang to appear voluntarily on 3 December, but also warned the panel could issue a subpoena to compel his testimony. Three House of Representatives committees - on intelligence and foreign affairs and a panel on China - have also sent a letter to Huang summoning him for a closed-door interview on 1 December. - How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions - Published12 hours ago - The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal - Published12 hours ago Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. - Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently? - Published14 hours ago Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company. It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said. Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public. Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared. Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information. The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures. Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming. But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data. Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO. Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires. Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia. Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago. Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector. news.title: Australian footballers will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
news.summary: Four Sydney Swans players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Australian footballers will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
news.summaryTr: Four Sydney Swans players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.
news.articleText: Sydney Swans players will not be charged after hotel incident, police say - Published Four top Australian Football League (AFL) players who were investigated in relation to an alleged sexual assault at a hotel in Melbourne earlier this year will not be charged, police have said. After a "thorough investigation and based on legal advice" police would not proceed with criminal charges due to "insufficient evidence", police said in a statement. Four Sydney Swans players - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, who now plays for North Melbourne - had been suspended for the rest of the season over the incident in August. The men previously denied wrongdoing but apologised for breaching club standards by inviting women back to the hotel after a game and drinking. Australian media reported that three women, understood to be adult entertainers, had alleged inappropriate touching during the incident at the Pullman Hotel and are looking into civil action. "Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment," police said in a statement on Friday. A fifth player, Riley Bice, who was also suspended by the club, had already been cleared by police. A lawyer for one of the women said she was "devastated" by the police decision. Jackson Pannam, of Slater and Gordon law firm, added that the move "does not amount to a finding that the incident our client reported did not occur, nor does it diminish the seriousness of what she says happened or its profound impact on her". John Karantzis from Carbone Lawyers, acting for the other two women, told the ABC his clients were "very disappointed and distressed". They would "vigorously pursue" a civil action, he said. "My clients' civil claim is based on a different burden of proof, it is based on the balance of probabilities," he said. Heeney welcomed the police announcement, saying the past three months had been "incredibly difficult for my family, [my fiancee] Steffie and those close to me". "To my family and friends, your love and loyalty has meant more than words can do justice," he continued. The Swans said in a statement that it had been "clear from the outset" that its decision to suspend the players was "separate from the police investigation, and it stands by that decision". "The Club has commenced a comprehensive examination of its AFL program and is committed to acting on the findings and implementing meaningful change to build an environment that players, staff, members, supporters and corporate partners can be proud of," it said. Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich told reporters it was "not a day for anyone to really celebrate" and "we're still looking very hard at the programme and understanding where we need to get better". He said the club would be doing everything to "restore the standards that this club has held for a long period of time". In a separate statement the AFL acknowledged the police decision and said it reserved the right to investigate should any further relevant information come to light.

news.summary: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.

news.titleTr: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
news.summaryTr: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.
news.articleText: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI - Published State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say. More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau. "The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman. This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from the company. US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim. Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software. According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet. Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction. A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims. Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities. The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user". "It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday. "If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

news.summary: The White House also named a former CFTC commissioner and two CLARITY Act veterans as nominees to fill vacancies at the SEC and CFTC.

news.titleTr: Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks
news.summaryTr: The White House also named a former CFTC commissioner and two CLARITY Act veterans as nominees to fill vacancies at the SEC and CFTC.
news.articleText: Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks The White House also named a former CFTC commissioner and two CLARITY Act veterans as nominees to fill vacancies at the SEC and CFTC. US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation. The nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC currently has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission. The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks. Related: House Finance panel chair says regulator actions on crypto ‘fall short’ of CLARITY bill Levine, a Republican, was nominated for an SEC term ending June 5, 2030, replacing Peirce, who left the agency in October. Peirce was a leading advocate for clearer crypto rules at the SEC, helping shape its approach to digital assets as the former head of its Crypto Task Force, while Levine’s views on crypto regulation are less publicly established. Trump also nominated Democrat Kristin Johnson, a former CFTC commissioner, for the SEC seat held by Caroline Crenshaw, whose term has also expired. Johnson’s proposed term ends June 5, 2029. Johnson has advocated for stronger customer protections and conflict-of-interest rules for crypto firms in her time at the CFTC. For the CFTC, Trump nominated Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland, both of whom worked on the Clarity Act. CFTC Chairman Mike Selig called them “two strong bipartisan picks” for CFTC commissioners and said he looked forward to working with them upon their confirmation. The nominees would typically appear before the Senate Banking Committee for the SEC positions and the Senate Agriculture Committee for the CFTC roles. Following committee consideration, their nominations would go to the full Senate, where confirmation requires a majority vote. Magazine: Can the SEC and CFTC’s pro-crypto rules be overturned? news.title: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
news.summary: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
news.summaryTr: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.
news.articleText: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks - Published Ukraine's president has welcomed a pledge from US envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, to include delegates from the European Union in the next round of peace talks with Russia. European leaders have expressed deepening security concerns this week, and Volodymyr Zelensky said bringing them into the talks would ensure the EU has a "voice" in negotiations. Kushner and Witkoff met Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday evening as part of a busy day of shuttle diplomacy - they met Vladimir Putin in Moscow earlier, who said that Russia's position on the war - and its demand for territory - has not changed. The meetings follow talks in Abu Dhabi last week that failed to reach a breakthrough in ending the war. But Thursday did see Russia and Ukraine agree to another prisoner exchange - the largest swap yet since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. Kushner said it would return "thousands of people to their families", but further details like how many prisoners would be exchanged or a timeline, were not given. - US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow - Published8 hours ago - Europe's security 'fundamentally reshaped' by war in Ukraine - Published14 hours ago Zelensky has for several years been calling for European delegates to be included in the peace talks, and says it makes sense because of Kyiv's longer-term ambition to join the European Union. On Thursday, Kushner said that the US has been "working very, very closely over the past several months with Europeans and I think that that's been very important." He added that he had stressed to Putin how important it is to have European delegates "at the table". "He's willing to give it a try," Kushner added. Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US government's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin. Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent. Earlier on Thursday, Vice President of the European Commission Kaja Kallas, the EU's top diplomat, told BBC's Newshour the presence of a European delegate showed the Kremlin "now realised that Europe is a big player". Kallas also expressed doubts that there was Russian momentum towards a peace deal. Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) Micheál Martin told a host of Euro leaders gathered in the Irish capital on Thursday that he believed the security of the region has been "fundamentally reshaped" by Russia's war. "Many member states [of the EU] feel an existential threat because of what has happened in Ukraine and the potential, if Ukraine was to fall, for further aggression on the European continent," he told reporters. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine remains under control of Russian forces, and cross-border incursions are increasingly common. Tensions between the US and Ukraine were on display on Thursday before Witkoff and Kushner's meeting with Zelensky. Earlier, the Ukrainian leader said that the military was facing more "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones. The technology owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX company has played a vital role in government and military connectivity in Ukraine, and increasingly assists in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line.

Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) Micheál Martin told a host of Euro leaders gathered in the Irish capital on Thursday that he believed the security of the region has been "fundamentally reshaped" by Russia's war. "Many member states [of the EU] feel an existential threat because of what has happened in Ukraine and the potential, if Ukraine was to fall, for further aggression on the European continent," he told reporters. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine remains under control of Russian forces, and cross-border incursions are increasingly common. Tensions between the US and Ukraine were on display on Thursday before Witkoff and Kushner's meeting with Zelensky. Earlier, the Ukrainian leader said that the military was facing more "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones. The technology owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX company has played a vital role in government and military connectivity in Ukraine, and increasingly assists in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line.

news.title: Former Nvidia CEO Huang had third alleged affair: Reuters
news.summary: Reuters reported that Jensen Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee, hours after he resigned as CEO.

news.titleTr: Former Nvidia CEO Huang had third alleged affair: Reuters
news.summaryTr: Reuters reported that Jensen Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee, hours after he resigned as CEO.
news.articleText: Former Nvidia CEO Huang had third alleged affair: Reuters Reuters reported that Jensen Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee, hours after he resigned as CEO. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second company employee, Reuters reported, bringing the number of alleged extramarital affairs to three. The report, citing two people familiar with the matter, followed Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO and a board member on Thursday. Reuters did not identify the other employee in its report and said attempts to reach her were unsuccessful. The two previously reported relationships involved Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials suspect of working for Chinese intelligence, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care. Cointelegraph reached out to Nvidia for comment. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said Thursday during a press conference that the Justice Department had not determined whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. He confirmed that the FBI was investigating reports that she worked for the Chinese government. Beijing has denied the allegations. Nvidia shares fell more than 13% shortly after the US market opened on Thursday, trading at $151.00 as of 2:31 p.m. UTC, according to Yahoo Finance. Venture capitalist Haseeb Qureshi argued that the mounting disclosures undermined Huang’s credibility, pushing back against tech industry figures defending the Nvidia co-founder. “As others have said: ‘when you find two ants in your kitchen, the best estimate for the ants in your kitchen is not two,’” Qureshi wrote on X. Related: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, exits board; shares plunge

news.title: Gemini’s quarterly retail trading volume sinks to 3-year low
news.summary: Gemini’s third-quarter trading rebound masked a deepening retail slump.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Gemini’s quarterly retail trading volume sinks to 3-year low
news.summaryTr: Gemini’s third-quarter trading rebound masked a deepening retail slump.
news.articleText: Gemini’s quarterly retail trading volume sinks to 3-year low Gemini’s third-quarter trading rebound masked a deepening retail slump. Crypto exchange Gemini has just reported its lowest quarterly retail trading volume in three years, despite an increase in overall crypto trading volume. Total spot trading volume rose 18% from the second quarter to $4.5 billion, according to Gemini’s Q3 earnings report. Institutional volume climbed 26% to $3.9 billion, while retail volume fell 14% to $600 million, its lowest level since the third quarter of 2023. Gemini said the quarterly increase in spot trading volume was “supported by increased institutional Zcash activity and expanded affiliated market-making,” but did not give a specific reason for the decline in retail trading. Despite the retail slump, Gemini’s exchange revenue increased 7% from the previous quarter to $13.4 million as institutional revenue more than doubled. Retail traders remained its largest source of exchange revenue, contributing nearly three-quarters of the total. Crypto exchanges turn to prediction markets for growth A number of crypto exchanges also reported softer crypto trading activity in the most recent quarter. Coinbase reported softer retail and institutional activity, with consumer spot trading volume falling 9% from the previous quarter to $23.4 billion. Coinbase chief financial officer Alesia Haas said “continued growth in prediction markets helped offset softer crypto trading activity.” At Robinhood, crypto revenue fell 55% year-on-year to $120 million, offset by a sixfold increase in event-contract revenue to $173 million. Related: Strategy stock sheds 5% amid MSCI index removal, Bitcoin sell-off Gemini also got some help from its own prediction exchange, Gemini Predictions, with revenue from that business unit increasing 52% quarter-on-quarter to $796,000, though it wasn’t significant enough to offset declines elsewhere. Gemini looks to expand prediction markets Gemini reported stronger prediction-market activity heading into the fourth quarter, with average daily traders in October running about 50% above the third-quarter average. Nearly a third of new prediction traders were new to Gemini, more than double the proportion in Q3. The company is also seeking to distribute its event contracts through other platforms. An August nonbinding agreement with Apex Fintech Solutions would make Gemini Titan the exclusive venue for crypto event contracts distributed through Apex’s futures brokerage to its brokerage customers, subject to definitive agreements. Gemini is set to host a Q3 earnings call on Friday. Magazine: NK hackers join memecoin trenches, xStocks adds Hong Kong equities: Asia Express

news.title: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
news.summary: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
news.summaryTr: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.
news.articleText: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over? - Published Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment. "People can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC. After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter. "Things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion. Above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next." Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022. But within less than two weeks, federal forces marched triumphantly into Mekelle. The TPLF made what it called a "strategic withdrawal" from the city and Tigray's other main towns so the army encountered little resistance. Hundreds of people are reported to have died in the conflict, including dozens killed by drone strikes and bombing raids by the air force. Ethiopian government officials and supporters argue that the war is effectively over and that the only remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements. Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who switched sides and is now an adviser to the prime minister, declared that the war in Tigray had ended and that stabilising the region should now be the immediate priority. Cameroon Hudson, an analyst and consultant on African peace and security, says there are various reasons for the TPLF's rapid defeat. "The TPLF has lost popular support at home. It is fragmented, it does not possess the advanced military technology necessary to match the ENDF [Ethiopian National Defence Forces]," he says. "It has lost many of its generals, strategic thinkers, finest diplomats and fighters, either through defections or arrests. The infighting within the TPLF leadership has caused significant damage." Abraha Hailezgi, a scholar at Mekelle University, agrees. "The army lacks a clear political vision. In recent years, it has become associated with coercion, abuses, forced recruitment and arbitrary actions. As a result, many people have come to view the TPLF army as an adversary rather than a force acting on their behalf," he says. Speaking by telephone from an undisclosed location, TPLF spokesperson Mikael Asgedom denies that the group has lost. Instead, he describes it as a deliberate tactical and strategic retreat. "This is not a defeat," he tells the BBC. He says the TPLF "intentionally allowed the ENDF to advance deeper into the heartland of Tigray", where it can be isolated and confronted on favourable terrain. "We chose not to fight on terms favourable to the enemy." The TPLF is preparing for a major counteroffensive, he says, adding that TPLF fighters have launched attacks against Ethiopian forces in several locations following their withdrawal from the region's towns, arguing that these operations demonstrated the group's continued military capability. It is hard to get verified information from Tigray and the BBC is unable to report from there. But phone lines and the internet, which were cut when fighting broke out, have now been restored. Residents in different parts of Tigray tell the BBC that fighting is continuing in central, northern and north-western parts of Tigray, with the use of heavy artillery and drone strikes. Eyewitnesses around Sheraro, a town near the Eritrean border, report heavy fighting involving artillery and ground forces in recent days. "We could hear heavy artillery fire from the Sheraro direction. People are concerned because there is no sense of security," a businessman tells the BBC on condition of anonymity. He adds that military convoys from both sides had moved towards Sheraro, while a motorcycle operator in the southern town of Yechila says military checkpoints are still active. Memories of the devastating 2020-2022 Tigray war remain raw for many residents. The conflict saw widespread human rights abuses and allegations of ethnic cleansing in Western Tigray, while estimates suggest the war claimed hundreds of thousands of lives. As soldiers from Eritrea, accused of some of the worst atrocities in the previous conflict, and Ethiopia have reappeared in Tigray's towns, many residents describe a profound sense of fear and anxiety, saying the sight of the troops has reopened still-fresh wounds. Military sources aligned with the federal army say operations against the TPLF are continuing, with recent fighting and troop movements reported in northern Tigray, near the Eritrean border, as well as across central Tigray's rugged highlands. They claim the TPLF's capabilities are being steadily degraded. Security analysts and observers agree that unrest is likely to continue for some time. "I see a situation in which there could be a prolonged war in Tigray," Yared Tibebu, a well-known Ethiopian commentator based in the US, tells the BBC. Yared argues that the TPLF has a long history of waging protracted armed struggles and believes the movement is once again preparing for a lengthy conflict. He believes that once the group has reorganised its military and political structures, it may attempt to resume offensive operations. However he believes this will not happen for some time because of internal divisions - a suggestion dismissed by TPLF spokesperson Mikael. Hudson rejects the idea that Tigray is heading towards a prolonged war but agrees that the region may not be truly peaceful for some time. "The TPLF may continue a low-level insurgency and guerrilla campaign, but that is not war. I do not think there will be a wider-scale conflict between the federal forces and the TPLF." He says the TPLF no longer possesses the size, strength or military capability required to effectively confront federal forces, which he says have significantly expanded and modernised in recent years. "The TPLF has also lost much of its public support and cannot easily rebuild its ranks through recruitment," he says. Yared, on the other hand, points to the TPLF's history of overcoming setbacks as evidence that the movement could recover to sustain a prolonged struggle. "The TPLF has overcome many major challenges in the past. It is wrong to conclude that it has no public support. It is a political movement with a history stretching back more than 50 years," he says. What Yared sees as a strength, Hudson sees as a weakness, saying the TPLF is still "trapped in the past", and continues to behave as a dominant party within Tigray, even though the situation has changed. "It is a movement that has not evolved, modernised or expanded." While Hudson argues that the TPLF is not equipped to sustain a major military campaign, the TPLF spokesman says the group obtains weapons and logistical supplies from the Ethiopian military. "We seize weapons from our enemy, and the weaponry that has entered Tigray will, sooner or later, become ours." In early October, eyewitnesses told the BBC they had seen Eritrean troops in Tigray amid reports they were backing the TPLF. However, they appear to have returned home and Hudson thinks the country would be wary of becoming further embroiled in the conflict. "First, Eritrea does not have unlimited resources. Second, the TPLF is no more an effective military force, and Eritrean leaders may have concluded that supporting it at this stage would not yield significant military gains," he says. "Third, Eritrea would have to consider the risk of provoking a confrontation with Ethiopia if it openly backs the TPLF." Sources in the Ethiopia army tell the BBC that senior members of the TPLF's political leadership were briefly based in Eritrea, however, they say the authorities ordered them to leave in early November, shortly after President Isaias Afwerki returned from Russia. According to the sources, the move was driven by concerns that Ethiopia could use their presence as a reason to invade. Hudson also argues that Eritrea's renewed diplomatic engagement with the US, whose relations with the TPLF have long been strained, could further discourage Asmara from providing meaningful support to the movement. In September, seven Ethiopian rebel groups led by the TPLF announced the formation of a new coalition called the Alliance for Survival, aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government. Yared believes the alliance could give the TPLF the strength to keep on fighting. "Its members can combine their strengths. The TDF [the TPLF's military wing] has leadership experience and organisational capacity, while Fano [an ethnic Amhara militia] is believed to have between 70,000 and 80,000 fighters. "If conditions emerge that allow the forces to co-ordinate effectively, the TPLF's current difficulties may not last long," he says. Hudson, however, rejects that argument, insisting that the alliance is unlikely to alter the balance of power. "I don't think the TPLF can be saved by this alliance. The ethnic militias have not demonstrated the capacity, either individually or collectively, to pose a serious threat to federal forces. We should not underestimate the strength of the federal army," he says. Abraha from Mekelle University argues that the conflict in Tigray will only truly be over if the federal government addresses the region's feeling that it has been marginalised, both economically and politically by the current government. However, many Tigrayan elites and political observers remain wary of the federal government's intentions. They question whether the authorities in Addis Ababa are genuinely seeking to address Tigray's problems, or whether they are taking advantage of the region's weakness to boost their influence. In the meantime, many ordinary people in Tigray say their priority is peace. "Peace seems slow in coming. Most people are tired of politics. Whatever happens, we only want peace and a chance to rebuild our lives," says Firut from her beauty salon in Mekelle. news.titleTr: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading?
news.summaryTr: Experts warn that using AI to enhance property images can go too far and mislead prospective buyers.
news.articleText: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading? - Published Have you ever been impressed by the pictures of a property on an estate agent's website, only to find the place looks completely different when you view it in person? Then there's a chance that AI was used to enhance the images you saw. From repainted walls to imaginary lawns, estate agents are increasingly using the technology to make homes seem more appealing, arguing it helps buyers visualise the potential of a place. But experts warn it can go too far and mislead prospective buyers - a trend dubbed "housefishing". So how much AI enhancement is too much? 'The rooms were much smaller' Earlier this year Olivia Nicole, 29, was searching online for five-bedroom properties in south-west London when a house on Rightmove caught her eye. But when she arrived to view it several days later she initially thought she had come to the wrong place. "The rooms were much smaller than they were in the pictures and the decor was totally different," she tells the BBC. "Some structural features were also different." For example, there was a raised section of the wall behind the sofa that didn't appear in the images. The windows were also noticeably smaller. Olivia was so surprised she took her own pictures of the property for comparison. It later turned out the pictures she had seen on Rightmove, which also appeared on the Zoopla and Winkworth websites, were enhanced with AI. But that wasn't clear in the listing, Olivia says, and she feels the agent wasted her time. "It was frustrating, because I had taken several hours off work for the viewing which I had to make up for." All three companies told the BBC they had strict guidelines on how AI could be used on their websites and have since taken the images down. 'A surge of AI listings' Estate agents have long used wide-angle lens cameras or Photoshop to make homes seem bigger or more appealing to buyers, but AI is making this process much easier and more accessible. It is difficult to quantify how common the practice is, says the Guild of Property Professionals, a trade group of independent estate agents, but it has issued guidance on how to use AI enhancement responsibly. According to a recent survey, external of 906 UK homebuyers, one in five who had who purchased a home in the past year said they had viewed a property where the listing photos had been digitally enhanced to make the home appear better than it actually was. Jack Bushrod reviews quirky property listings he finds on Rightmove for his social media channel, Housing Horrors, and says he has seen a "surge" of AI-enhanced images over the last six months. He thinks using AI is fine up to a point - to declutter a busy room, or add furniture to an empty one so a prospective buyer can see its potential. But he draws the line at anything that misleads a prospective buyer or wastes their time. "I've seen one house where they had removed a pillar and added a window. Others might use AI to remove stains on the carpet or cracks in tiles. It's little details you would only notice in person." He says most of the enhanced images he's seen weren't clearly labelled as AI-generated. Cara, 38, is currently selling her home in Lowestoft, Suffolk, and says she was surprised when she saw the AI-enhanced pictures of her property her estate agent, Howards, put on Rightmove. In one photo, her son's room was completely emptied of toys and clutter. In another, of her daughter's room, the agent appears to have removed a doll's house, brightened the room, and used AI to change the shape of a rug, but that image has since been taken down. Cara has had several viewings so far and says that one person has commented on the differences. But she says she trusts Howards, which has acknowledged the use of AI in the property listing. "If they'd changed something structurally or it was really wild and didn't look like our home at all then I would put my foot down," she says. A spokeswoman told the BBC that Howards had now introduced a policy of labelling all AI-enhanced photos. She added that the firm never used AI "to misrepresent the fundamental features of a property". "It's about helping people imagine the possibilities, not changing the reality of what's being sold." 'Jumping on the bandwagon' Trading Standards told the BBC that estate agents can use AI to make basic enhancements to photos, or to virtually furnish an empty room or garden, as long as they indicate they have used the technology. But it says structurally changing a room, for example by adding a window, or hiding features could mislead consumers and break the law. Jack Bushrod thinks all estate agents should have to clearly label AI-enhanced photos and mention any use of the tech prominently in the key features slide of a property listing. He also expects to see more housefishing as time goes on. "My worry is the more estate agents use AI, others will see the trend and jump on the bandwagon." Additional reporting by Star McFarlane Related topics - Published18 September - Published3 November

news.articleText: Military cemetery decorum: The tradition behind Hegseth's Veterans Day reprimand Earlier this week, a sentinel reprimanded a group that included US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at Arlington National Cemetery. The incident followed a wreath-laying ceremony marking Veterans Day. The Pentagon have since announced that Hegseth has given the soldier, Specialist Thomas Iglesias, a Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier". BBC's Bernd Debusmann breaks down why Hegseth's group was reprimanded, the history behind the strict rules governing visitor behaviour and the importance of maintaining an atmosphere of silence at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

news.summary: Maple Finance co-founder Joe Flanagan and COO Ryan O’Shea are leaving over disagreements about the firm’s direction as SYRUP falls despite revenue growth.

news.titleTr: Maple Finance’s strategy rift sends co-founder, COO to the exits
news.summaryTr: Maple Finance co-founder Joe Flanagan and COO Ryan O’Shea are leaving over disagreements about the firm’s direction as SYRUP falls despite revenue growth.
news.articleText: Maple Finance’s strategy rift sends co-founder, COO to the exits Maple Finance co-founder Joe Flanagan and COO Ryan O’Shea are leaving over disagreements about the firm’s direction as SYRUP falls despite revenue growth. Two senior executives are leaving onchain asset manager Maple Finance over disagreements about the firm’s direction as its SYRUP token slid more than 7% Thursday. Maple co-founder and executive chairman Joe Flanagan said Wednesday he would leave after seven years at the firm, describing a growing divide with fellow co-founder and CEO Sidney Powell. “Over time, our views on strategy, leadership, and life have moved further apart,” Flanagan wrote. “I believe Maple is best served by one co-founder leading it forward from here.” Chief operating officer Ryan O’Shea also said in a Thursday post on X that he would leave after nearly five years at Maple. “I’ll be stepping down as COO. I’ve come to a different view on the direction Maple should take, and I’ve decided it’s time to step aside,” he wrote. SYRUP traded at $0.12 at 10:36 p.m. UTC Thursday, down 7.5% over 24 hours and 12% over the past week, according to CoinGecko. The token had a market capitalization of about $145 million. Maple and Powell did not respond to Cointelegraph’s requests for comment by publication. Maple says leadership shakeup will not disrupt anything In a statement published Wednesday, Maple confirmed that Flanagan was stepping down as chairman and leaving the company. “This is an agreed and orderly transition,” the company said, adding that his responsibilities would move to Powell and Maple’s existing leadership team. The company did not announce a replacement chairman or specify how the departing executives’ duties would be carried out. Flanagan said his differences with Powell reached a point where they were no longer constructive. “I am choosing to leave rather than continue supporting a direction I cannot stand behind,” he said. Flanagan added that he would help with the transition through the end of 2026. O’Shea is stepping down effective Nov. 27. “I’ll have no ongoing role after that,” he wrote. The departures come as Maple looks to expand beyond crypto-backed lending. In October, Powell said the firm planned to reach more customers through fintech partnerships and lend against a wider range of assets, including payments owed on loans made by fintech companies and securities backed by assets such as mortgages. Related: Kraken, Maple launch onchain warehouse facility for crypto-backed institutional loans Revenue growth continues The announcements come as Maple’s lending business continues to grow, while SYRUP is down 62% year to date and total value locked (TVL) has declined. According to Token Terminal, Maple’s protocol revenue rose 8% year over year in October, while TVL fell around 11% between the end of September and Nov. 11. Maple’s latest quarterly results also showed growth, with the company reporting $4.4 million in third-quarter revenue, up 5% from a year earlier. Assets under management rose 18% year over year to $4.7 billion. Maple has also been using some of its revenue to buy back SYRUP tokens. In September, the company repurchased about 1.37 million tokens, twice as many as in August, according to its October update. Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

news.titleTr: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
news.summaryTr: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
news.articleText: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say - Published Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to under a radical overhaul of the welfare system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review. As reported in the Times,, external Alan Milburn's year-long report, to be published on Tuesday, is expected to recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits. Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 16 to 24 year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet". He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants. His report is expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide universal credit - or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales. Disabled people in Scotland can claim the devolved Adult Disability Payment. Instead, under Milburn's plan, under-25s would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit. Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions. Some claimants would receive less under the plans - although the exact amounts will not be clear until early next year, when the government publishes legislation to implement the changes. People can claim Pip to help them with the additional cost of being disabled or living with long-term physical or mental health conditions. It is available to those both in and out of work. In his interim report,, external Milburn said survey data found that 19% of young people claiming disability or health benefits were in work. Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers. Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate. Milburn told the Times: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system. "But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances. "I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around." Speaking later on Thursday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said young people would be given support "when they need it as teenagers rather than leaving them on benefits in their 20s". He added: "The principle that we will be working on is that we will guarantee support for young people and that is the whole basis on which we will proceed." Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets, data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests. This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year. Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare changes last year under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer. Dame Meg Hillier, who helped spearhead a backbench rebellion against Starmer's reforms, suggested she and her colleagues were broadly supportive this time around. "What happened last year was a cut was being proposed and none of us could explain to people what would happen to them," the Labour MP told the BBC. "Milburn has done some very good work on this so I'm giving him a fair wind," she added. But Bell Ribeiro-Addy, one of the Labour backbenchers who revolted last year, said she was "not sure" she could vote to cut the benefit entitlement of existing claimants. 'Cannot assume' Tom Ashforth, a 19-year-old student at Sheffield Hallam University, receives both components of Pip at the higher rate. He said the financial support helps him manage additional expenses linked to his visual impairment, including prescriptions, mobility aids and accessible learning resources. "If I were to lose it, I would struggle to afford essential things," he said. He said he believes decisions over disability benefits should be made on a case-by-case basis, rather than according to age. "You cannot assume that everyone under the age of 25 is in the same position," he said. In his Times interview, Milburn acknowledged that changing the rules for existing claimants would be "difficult politically" but stressed it was necessary. 'Rebuilding system from scratch' James Taylor, from disability equality charity Scope, said Pip was a "lifeline" and restricting access to it "won't make young disabled people's extra costs disappear". Harriet Edwards, from the charity Sense, said changes were "long overdue", but that without additional details, families were "deeply anxious". A government spokesperson said: "We will always ensure there is a safety net for the most vulnerable and those who are unable to work." The reforms would represent a radical overhaul of Britain's welfare system, at a time when there is heavy political pressure for the UK to find the money to spend more on defence. Both the Conservatives and Reform UK have argued for significant cuts to welfare, including to fund a boost to defence. Responding on Thursday, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the government should not be spending "lots of time" on employment schemes, which she said would ultimately fail. If Milburn's recommendations were approved, it could take almost a decade for the British state to see monetary savings. The new system "will need significant investment" and would involve "rebuilding the system from scratch", Milburn said. His new proposed system would involve an element of carrot and stick, wherein young people could lose some of their benefits if they did not engage with the extra work support options. In an interview recorded on Tuesday, Skills Minister Jacqui Smith told the BBC that young people had a "responsibility" to take up employment support. "It is a contract. People need the chance, and they need to take that chance," she added. A separate review - co-chaired by disabilities minister Sir Stephen Timms - examining disability benefits is also expected to be published this month. news.titleTr: Cevdet Yılmaz'dan COP31 mesajı: "Özel sektör olmadan iklim hedeflerine ulaşılamaz"
news.summaryTr: Antalya’da düzenlenen COP31 İş ve Yatırım Zirvesi’nde 55’i aşkın ülkeden bin 500’ün üzerinde katılımcı bir araya geldi. Zirvede iklim finansmanı, enerji güvenliği ve sanayinin yeşil dönüşümü öne çıkarken, iş dünyasının iklim hedeflerinin hayata geçirilmesindeki rolüne dikkat çekildi.
news.articleText: Cevdet Yılmaz'dan COP31 mesajı: "Özel sektör olmadan iklim hedeflerine ulaşılamaz" - Antalya'da düzenlenen COP31 İş ve Yatırım Zirvesi'nde 55'i aşkın ülkeden bin 500’ün üzerinde katılımcı bir araya geldi. - Zirvede iklim finansmanı, enerji güvenliği ve sanayinin yeşil dönüşümü öne çıkarken, iş dünyasının iklim hedeflerinin hayata geçirilmesindeki rolüne dikkat çekildi. Türkiye Odalar ve Borsalar Birliği (TOBB) koordinasyonunda düzenlenen COP31 İş ve Yatırım Zirvesi, 12 Kasım’da Antalya’da başladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle "Hedeften Uygulamaya" temasıyla gerçekleştirilen zirvede, iklim hedeflerinin yatırım projelerine dönüştürülmesi, enerji dönüşümü, sanayinin karbonsuzlaştırılması ve dirençli şehirler ele alındı. Zirvenin açılışında konuşan Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz, yeşil dönüşümün fosil yakıt ithalatını azaltarak makroekonomik istikrara katkı sağlayacağını belirtti. İklim hedeflerine ulaşılması için finansmana hazır projelerin ve kamu-özel sektör iş birliğinin önemini vurgulayan Yılmaz, özel sektörün sürece dahil edilmediği iklim politikalarının başarılı olamayacağını söyledi. COP31 Başkanı ve Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanı Murat Kurum ise zirveyi bir “uygulama COP’u” olarak konumlandırdıklarını ifade etti. Kurum, 2035’e kadar nihai enerji tüketiminde elektriğin payını yüzde 35’e, üretim ve imalatta döngüsel malzeme kullanımını en az yüzde 15’e çıkarma hedeflerini açıkladı. İklim Uygulama Köprüsü aracılığıyla ülkelerin önceliklerini yatırım yapılabilir projelere dönüştürmeyi amaçladıklarını belirtti. Hisarcıklıoğlu: "İklim eylemi en büyük yatırım fırsatı" TOBB Başkanı ve COP31 İş Forumu Başkanı Rifat Hisarcıklıoğlu, iklim hedeflerine müzakere salonlarında değil, fabrikalarda, tarlalarda ve şantiyelerde ulaşılabileceğini söyledi. İş dünyasının iklim eylemi açısından merkezi bir rol üstlendiğini belirten Hisarcıklıoğlu, iklim eyleminin bir maliyet değil, neslin en büyük yatırım fırsatı olduğunu vurguladı. Hisarcıklıoğlu, bu fırsatın hayata geçirilmesi için teknolojinin yanı sıra net ve istikrarlı politikalara, hızlı izin süreçlerine ve adil rekabete ihtiyaç duyulduğunu kaydetti. Dünya Bankası Başkanı'ndan özel sektör sermayesi vurgusu Zirvede düzenlenen oturumda konuşan Dünya Bankası Grubu Başkanı Ajay Banga, iklim yatırımlarının ekonomik getiriler ve genç istihdamı odağında değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini belirtti. BBVA Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Carlos Torres Vila ise gelişmekte olan ülkelerde KOBİ’lerin yeşil finansmana erişiminin önemine dikkat çekti. Vila, enerji verimliliği, elektrifikasyon, akıllı şebekeler ve yapay zekanın Türkiye gibi yüksek potansiyele sahip ülkelerin rekabet gücünü artırabileceğini ifade etti. Enerji güvenliği ve sanayinin dönüşümü gündemde Zirvenin oturumlarında enerji arz güvenliği, elektrifikasyon, iklim yatırımlarının finansmanı ve sanayinin karbonsuzlaştırılması da ele alındı. Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanı Alparslan Bayraktar, IEA İcra Direktörü Fatih Birol ve BBVA Grup CEO’su Onur Genç enerji güvenliğini değerlendirirken, Sanayi ve Teknoloji Bakanı Mehmet Fatih Kacır ile Sabancı Holding CEO’su Kıvanç Zaimler elektrifikasyon başlığında görüşlerini paylaştı. Londra Belediye Başkanı Sadiq Khan ise şehirlerin iklim mücadelesindeki rolüne dikkat çekerek, dünya nüfusunun yarısından fazlasının şehirlerde yaşadığını ve enerjinin yüzde 70’inden fazlasının şehirlerde tüketildiğini söyledi. Khan, şehirlerin iklim krizinde ya sorunun parçası ya da çözümün kendisi olabileceğini ifade etti. COP31 İş ve Yatırım Zirvesi, 13 Kasım’da döngüsel ekonomi, KOBİ’lerin yeşil dönüşümü, iklim teknolojileri ve COP32 sürecine ilişkin oturumlarla devam edecek.

news.title: NK hackers join memecoin trenches, xStocks adds Hong Kong equities: Asia Express
news.summary: North Korean hackers launch memecoins to launder funds stolen in the Binance hack, while xStocks plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: NK hackers join memecoin trenches, xStocks adds Hong Kong equities: Asia Express
news.summaryTr: North Korean hackers launch memecoins to launder funds stolen in the Binance hack, while xStocks plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks.
news.articleText: NK hackers join memecoin trenches, xStocks adds Hong Kong equities: Asia Express North Korean hackers launch memecoins to launder funds stolen in the Binance hack, while xStocks plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks. North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move $430,000 of stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. However, the tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch. Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain. HONG KONG Hong Kong’s wealthy investors are embracing crypto. (Chi Hung Wong) xStocks tokenizes 200 stocks in UK and EU, with hundreds from Hong Kong coming soon Kraken parent Payward’s xStocks platform has added tokenized versions of more than 200 stocks listed in the United Kingdom and European Union. Payward said the latest expansion brings xStocks’ offering to more than 1,500 tokenized assets. The company reported more than $45 billion in cumulative transaction volume and over 550,000 unique holders. Payward said it plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks. Hong Kong’s forthcoming crypto licensing regime Deputy Secretary for Financial Services Chan Ho-lim told FinTech Week the region will introduces a new licensing regime for virtual-asset trading, custody, advisory and management, via amendment bills that will be submitted to Legislative Council this year. More Hong Kong news Police have arrested 22 people in a cross border money laundering investigation, that allegedly involved a over the counter crypto network that moved more than HKD$150 million (US$18 million) while attempting to obscure the origin of funds. Meanwhile, the US has sanctioned 41 entities allegedly linked to the Cambodia’s Prince Group, including a man named Qiu Yong, who is accused of running Hong Kong companies on behalf of the criminal organization. SOUTH KOREA South Korea to permit crypto withdrawal freezes during hacking threats South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) plans to allow crypto exchanges to suspend deposits and withdrawals when hacking is suspected, rather than waiting until a breach is confirmed. The FSC said it would issue a no-action letter permitting preventive suspensions under certain conditions. Current rules prohibit exchanges from blocking withdrawals without legitimate grounds and explicitly allow restrictions only when a hacking incident is clearly established. The regulator also called for round-the-clock monitoring and incident response, higher cold-wallet holdings, and stronger insurance coverage and reserves. GOPAX puts everything on ice South Korean crypto exchange GOPAX announced on November 6 it was suspending trading, deposits and withdrawals and moving all user assets to cold wallets. The firm had received threatening emails that claimed a hack was imminent, and took the drastic step of putting everything on ice on the recommendation of financial authorities. JAPAN Nomura explores sale of crypto unit Laser Digital Japanese financial services giant Nomura Holdings is reportedly weighing a sale of its cryptocurrency subsidiary Laser Digital as Nomura’s European operations continue to post losses. Nomura has held talks with potential buyers, including Marex Group but is yet to make a final decision and could keep the business. Nomura’s European businesses posted a pretax loss of 7.4 billion yen ($46.5 million) in the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, their fourth consecutive quarterly loss. The company posted pretax profits in every other reporting region over the same period. THAILAND Thailand is examining new rules for ETFs and ICO investors (Sasint) Thailand proposes $148K daily cap on stablecoin deposits and withdrawals Thailand’s securities regulator has proposed capping daily stablecoin deposits and withdrawals at 5 million baht ($148,000) each per customer at regulated crypto operators. The limit would apply separately to deposits and withdrawals at each operator, Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said in a Thursday announcement. The regulator said the rules aim to curb money laundering, cybercrime and attempts to bypass cross-border money transfer rules. The draft would bar stablecoin transfers to and from third-party wallets. More Thailand news Thailand’s SEC will block access to Bitget from December 5. It has also proposed new tests for retail investors before allowing them to invest in ICOs. The tests would require knowledge of at least six areas including digital tokens and investor rights, blockchain technology, digital-asset wallets and distribution channels. The proposals will be up for comment until November 25. The SEC is also seeking feedback on new rules around margin loans and ETFs, but has ruled out allowing leveraged or crypto ETFs at this stage. Vietnam South Korean crypto firm Bithumb Asset, has invested $85 million into a luxury resort project in Hoi An in Vietnam being built by local real estate developer Asia Estate. Da Nang police have issued a warning about scams via “ghost” cryptocurrency projects that are really just ponzi schemes in disguise. They highlighted a fraud ring involving the DRK cryptocurrency project, led by Huynh Duc Van, 33, and seven accomplices, which was recently dealt with by law enforcement. SINGAPORE Nomura’s former head of crypto derivatives trading, John Kim, has joined Chicago-based DV Trading in Singapore to lead a new discretionary crypto-trading team. A Singapore woman lost S$78,000 (US$60,391) in a four-month long crypto scam after someone posing as an insurance buyer “helped” her to set up a crypto wallet. She initially believed she was making money, before getting cleared out after she was directed to the little known Qevorinex platform. International bank communication network Swift argued at Singapore FinTech Festival for shared standards to prevent digital assets from fragmenting across incompatible systems.

news.title: Trump'tan Küba'ya gözdağı: "Görev sürem bitmeden halletmek istiyorum"
news.summary: ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Küba'ya yönelik askeri müdahale seçeneğini dışlamadı. Trump, 2028'de görev süresi sona ermeden önce Küba meselesini çözmek istediğini söyledi.

news.titleTr: Trump'tan Küba'ya gözdağı: "Görev sürem bitmeden halletmek istiyorum"
news.summaryTr: ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Küba'ya yönelik askeri müdahale seçeneğini dışlamadı. Trump, 2028'de görev süresi sona ermeden önce Küba meselesini çözmek istediğini söyledi.
news.articleText: Trump'tan Küba'ya gözdağı: "Görev sürem bitmeden halletmek istiyorum" - ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Küba'ya yönelik askeri müdahale seçeneğini dışlamadı. Trump, 2028'de görev süresi sona ermeden önce Küba meselesini çözmek istediğini söyledi. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Küba'ya yönelik olası bir askeri operasyon hakkında açıklamalarda bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Salem News Channel'a telefonla bağlanan Trump, görev süresi dolmadan önce Küba meselesini halletmek istediğini belirtti. Küba'yı "başarısız bir ülke" olarak nitelendiren Trump, ABD Dışişleri Bakanı Marco Rubio'nun süreci iyi yönettiğini ve gelişmeleri yakından takip ettiklerini söyledi. Küba'ya askeri güç kullanılıp kullanılmayacağına ilişkin soruyu yanıtlayan Trump, sınırlı bir operasyon seçeneğine de açık olduğunu ifade etti. Trump, "Bunun için biraz askeri güç gerekse, zayıf bir operasyon olsa bile, sizin için sorun olur mu?" sorusuna, "Benim için uygundur, bunu kesinlikle değerlendiririm." yanıtını verdi. ABD ile Küba arasındaki ilişkiler, 1959 Küba Devrimi'nden bu yana ambargo ve siyasi gerilimlerle şekilleniyor. Washington yönetimi, 1960'lardan itibaren Küba'ya yönelik ekonomik yaptırımlar uyguluyor.

ABD ile Küba arasındaki ilişkiler, 1959 Küba Devrimi'nden bu yana ambargo ve siyasi gerilimlerle şekilleniyor. Washington yönetimi, 1960'lardan itibaren Küba'ya yönelik ekonomik yaptırımlar uyguluyor.

news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, Nvidia shares plunged after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and left the board. Coinbase’s head of EU policy said tighter DeFi rules could push users toward riskier platforms. Binance’s security chief warned about fake job interviews months before attackers used a similar tactic in the exchange’s $6.3 billion hack. Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, exits board; shares plunge Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president and CEO and stepped down from the company’s board on Thursday, effective immediately. The board named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO. Kress will retain her role as CFO while Nvidia’s board considers internal and external candidates for the permanent CEO role. The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones its first chair and said it expects Nvidia’s operations to proceed without interruption. Nvidia shares fell more than 13% shortly after the US market opened on Thursday, trading at $151.00 as of 2:31 p.m. UTC, according to Yahoo Finance. Bitcoin (BTC) fell alongside Nvidia shares, dropping as much as 3.5% to a multimonth low. The shares later pared losses to trade at $165 at 4:24 p.m. UTC, down 5% on the day. The stock was down more than 26% over the previous month. EU DeFi proposals could push users to riskier platforms, says Coinbase exec European Union efforts to tighten oversight of decentralized finance (DeFi) could drive crypto users toward platforms offering fewer investor protections, according to Coinbase’s head of EU policy. Roeland Van der Stappen told Cointelegraph that regulated crypto platforms could respond by limiting or dropping access to DeFi services. “Rules designed to protect investors would end up pushing activity towards the places with the least protection,” Van der Stappen said. In its September response to the European Commission’s consultation on the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), the European Securities and Markets Authority recommended creating a new category of regulated crypto services for firms that give customers access to DeFi protocols. Binance CSO unwittingly foreshadowed $6.3B hack tactic months before attack Months before Binance lost $6.3 billion to a hack, its chief security officer described to Cointelegraph how a fake job interview could give attackers a foothold inside the exchange — closely resembling one of the entry methods later used against the exchange. During a July interview about Binance’s response to rising security threats, Jimmy Su told Cointelegraph that fake job interviews were “something we worry about a lot internally,” explaining how attackers could tailor a job opportunity to an employee before persuading them to run code as part of a technical assessment. “And once that gets executed, the device is compromised and then they can start harvesting credentials,” Su said, adding that attackers could then use that to penetrate further into the network. Su’s detailed warning about malicious coding assessments was not included in Cointelegraph’s July coverage, but takes on new significance following the biggest crypto exchange hack in history.

news.title: Zayıflama ilaçlarında kalıcı görme kaybı riski: FDA'dan yeni uyarı
news.summary: FDA, Ozempic, Wegovy ve Mounjaro gibi popüler diyabet ve zayıflama ilaçlarının nadir ancak kalıcı görme kaybına yol açabilen bir göz rahatsızlığıyla ilişkili olabileceği uyarısıyla güvenlik etiketlerine yeni bilgiler eklenmesini istedi.
